name: Donation Checklist
description: A complete plan for what to donate, how to prep items, and where to give.

items.text: Collect items from each room into a central staging area
Sort into clothing, household, books, toys, and furniture
Separate donations from items to sell or recycle
items.note: Higher-value items may be worth selling instead.

items.text: Box each category together for easy drop-off
Keep an itemized list as you pack each box
Inspect each item for stains, tears, and heavy wear
Set aside anything broken, damaged, or unsafe
Test that electronics and appliances power on
Confirm sets and games include all their pieces
Recycle or toss items that fail the quality check
items.note: Only donate what you would give to a friend.

items.text: Match items to charities that accept that category
Check whether a local shelter or school needs specific goods
Confirm hours, locations, and any drop-off limits
Ask about free pickup for large furniture
items.note: Many charities collect bulky items at your door.

items.text: Pick a reputable organization you trust
Wash and fold clothing and linens
Wipe down dishes, toys, and small appliances
Bundle cords and small parts with their main item
Bag pairs of shoes together so they stay matched
Pack fragile items with padding to prevent breakage

sections.title: Drop Off and Get a Receipt

items.text: Load boxes into the car the night before drop-off
Schedule the trip so donations actually leave the house
Hand items to staff and request a written receipt
Record the date, charity, and estimated item values
items.note: Photograph higher-value donations for your records.

items.text: File the receipt with your tax documents
Update your donation log with what you gave
Note any items the charity declined for next time
Keep a donation box going for ongoing decluttering
Schedule a seasonal donation run on the calendar
Apply a one-in, one-out rule to keep clutter down
items.note: Drop new outgrown items straight into the box.

faq.a: Most charities accept clean clothing, shoes, books, working small appliances, kitchenware, toys, and gently used furniture. Always confirm an item is in good, usable condition first.
Skip broken, stained, or unsafe items, recalled goods, expired products, and anything heavily worn. Donating unusable items just shifts disposal costs onto the charity.

faq.q: How do I prepare items for donation?
faq.a: Wash clothing and linens, wipe down household goods, test that electronics work, and bundle small parts together. Clean, ready-to-use items are far more likely to find a new home.

faq.q: How do I get a tax receipt for donations?
faq.a: Ask for a written receipt at drop-off and keep an itemized list with estimated values. For larger donations, note the charity's details and date so your records support a deduction.

faq.q: Can I print this donation checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Download the printable PDF, keep it with your donation boxes, and check off each step so you sort, prep, and drop off items without forgetting your receipt.
